rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verses argue for judgement from moral principles and evidence within and outside human beings; this verse presents the rejecters’ objection.
rows.anchor: arguments relating to morals and morality as well as the ones found within man and outside him in support of the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters say human existence is limited to worldly life: after death, everything ends.
rows.anchor: their existence is confined to this worldly life only; after this life, there is no life or death

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They attribute death to time’s fortunes rather than God, comparing human lives to a tree that sprouts, matures, then withers.
rows.anchor: the fortunes of time which destroys them and not God; just as a tree sprouts and reaches its culmination and then becomes dry

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says their claim lacks knowledge and is speculation; they voice it to avoid limits on freedom and luxury.
rows.anchor: whatever they say is not based on knowledge; it is mere speculation and conjecture; they do not want to believe in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter follows from God’s power, wisdom, mercy, providence, and justice; without it creation would be purposeless amusement.
rows.anchor: The Hereafter is a consequence of God’s power, wisdom, mercy, providence and justice. If it does not come into being, then this world becomes merely a place of sport and amusement.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some infer from the verse that a group of Arab atheists denied God and the Hereafter; Islahi rejects this as a group description.
rows.anchor: Some people have deduced from this verse that there was a group of atheists in Arabia which denied God and the Hereafter. In my view, this is not correct.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says Arabs were polytheists, not a group of pure materialists: they doubted resurrection and expected their deities to secure rank and protect them from God.
rows.anchor: The Arabs were not those who denied these realities; they were polytheists

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time-fortunes claim does not deny God; Quraysh used it to counter the Qur’an’s warning that earlier peoples were destroyed for error, wrongdoing, and rejecting messengers.
rows.anchor: Their statement that the fortunes of time destroy them does not insinuate God’s denial; by these words, they only wanted to refute the philosophy of history

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh’s alternative history portrayed nations as passing away through time regardless of beliefs or deeds, easing the warning that their own fate could match earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: people are only destroyed because of the fortunes of time; a person is born, he grows up, reaches old age and then dies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their philosophy is unsupported conjecture built to sanction desires; intellect, human nature, the world, prophets, and sages support the Qur’anic teaching.
rows.anchor: it is mere speculation on which they have built the edifice of this philosophy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage closes with sorrow that people let conjecture guide them in a matter of such consequence.
rows.anchor: This style of discourse expresses great yearning and sorrow: very unfortunate are these people who have made their thoughts and conjectures to be their guides

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Qur’anic proofs of the Hereafter are recited, the rejecters’ sole counter is to demand that the Prophet and believers restore their dead ancestors.
rows.anchor: the only argument they have to negate it is their demand

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling this response their argument is sarcastic: it has no logical connection to the issue and is only a baseless notion.
rows.anchor: Out of arrogance they would regard it to be a conclusive argument; for this reason, the Qur’ān has sarcastically called it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source notes a similar challenge in al-‘Ankabūt: the people demand that God’s punishment be brought if the claim is true.
rows.anchor: the only answer of their nation would be

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to remind them that God alone gives life and death and will gather everyone for the certain Day of Judgement.
rows.anchor: Who gives them life and He alone Who gives them death; then He will gather them and this gathering together will continue till the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God’s power to give life and death is evident, asking whether He can recreate the dead is needless.
rows.anchor: when life and death are in the hands of God and this is a fact that cannot be denied, then the question whether He can recreate after giving death is needless

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe’s existence demonstrates one prevailing will, excluding the alleged duality of separate powers that give life and death.
rows.anchor: This could only have been possible if someone had the ability to give life and some other to give death. Inalienable proofs show that this universe is devoid of this duality.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gathering and judgement are necessary to make life and death purposeful rather than a meaningless creation.
rows.anchor: if after these, a day of accountability does not come, then the whole universe becomes a meaningless and purposeless creation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition after ‘gather you’ conveys continuity until Judgement Day, implying no one will be resurrected before it and undercutting the demand to raise ancestors now.
rows.anchor: expresses continuity and proximity; ie. this gathering together will continue till the Day of Judgement. It is evident from this that before the Day of Judgement, no one will be raised up

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because sovereignty over heaven and earth belongs to God alone, alleged deities cannot influence His decisions or rescue their adherents.
rows.anchor: To God alone belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; no one can dare influence His decisions.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts every community on its knees, summoned to its deeds register and told it will be recompensed for its conduct.
rows.anchor: every group will be sitting on its knees with legs folded to hear the verdict; each group will be called towards its record of deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ‘you see’ is singular, contextual evidence makes the address general, and all people will attend without exception.
rows.anchor: here contextual evidence shows that this is the case here too

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering includes believers and disbelievers, the righteous and wrongdoers; no one is exempt.
rows.anchor: disbelievers, righteous as well as wrong-doers will be gathered

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexicographers explain the posture of jathiyah as sitting on both knees, as slaves, subordinates, and criminals did before masters awaiting judgement.
rows.anchor: Slaves, subordinates and criminals used to sit before their masters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘book’ is the register recording the deeds of communities and nations; the author says its named registers will be discussed in al-Taṭfīf.
rows.anchor: this book will contain the record of deeds of groups and nations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘it will be said to them’ is elided before ‘today’ because context supplies it; each community hears it will be paid for its deeds.
rows.anchor: on account of contextual indication

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who did no good and relied on polytheism or intercession for a blissful future will instead find deprivation.
rows.anchor: a person who did not do good deeds and only dreamt of a blissful future on the basis of polytheism and intercession will find nothing but deprivation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record bears true witness without injustice or oversight because angels have written each person’s deeds at God’s behest.
rows.anchor: there is no possibility of any injustice or oversight from this register; it will truly and faithfully tell them what each person did

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who did good are admitted to God’s mercy, receiving abundant blessing; this is the clear triumph rather than worldly luxury.
rows.anchor: not only will these people be rewarded because of their deeds, they will be immensely blessed by Him as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fate of disbelievers receives more detail because this sūrah focuses on them, especially the arrogant; the question is a humiliating rebuke, not a request for an answer.
rows.anchor: This sūrah specifically deals with them; in particular, with the arrogant among them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance and persistence in sin despite warnings echo the earlier account in this sūrah, and the question is posed to rebuke and humiliate them.
rows.anchor: they showed arrogance and persisted on their sins in spite of God’s warnings and reminders

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reply that they know nothing of the Hour reveals they entertain the idea but demand complete certainty before believing.
rows.anchor: as far as the thought was concerned, these disbelievers did have it in their hearts; however, their demand was that only when they are fully convinced about it, then they will believe in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand to see dead ancestors is absurd: accepting only observable realities would discard reason and moral knowledge.
rows.anchor: Obviously, this was an absurd demand. It meant that a person will only believe in that thing which he can see from his eyes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At best, a person may be unable to believe in the Hereafter as an eyewitness event, but this does not establish that there is no Hereafter.
rows.anchor: At best, what a person can say is that he cannot believe in it the way he can believe an eye-witness happening

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At best, a person may be unable to believe in the Hereafter as an eyewitness event, but this does not establish that there is no Hereafter.
rows.anchor: At best, what a person can say is that he cannot believe in it the way he can believe an eye-witness happening

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequences of intellectual and moral sins are delayed, encouraging wrongdoers to mock warnings; on Judgement Day they will see the evil harvest and be overtaken by the punishment they mocked.
rows.anchor: On that Day, the blindest of people will see the horrible harvest of the seeds he had sown in the previous world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their past disregard for the messengers’ warnings is answered by God’s disregard of them on Judgement Day.
rows.anchor: they had ignored the warnings of the messengers of God and his righteous people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s disregard extends to ignoring their pleas; neither their companions nor the deities whose intercession they trusted will help them.
rows.anchor: However much may they plead and beseech Him, they will not receive any response to their imploring

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They merit God’s indifference because they mocked His verses and walked away from their recitation; this theme was raised earlier in verses 8–9.
rows.anchor: when His verses informing them of the Last Day would be recited out to them, they would make fun of them and would walk away from that place as if they had not heard a thing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mistook worldly affluence for proof that their beliefs and deeds were right, mocking less prosperous well-wishers who warned them.
rows.anchor: they concluded from the affluence and opulence God blessed them with in this world that they were worthy of these favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance leaves no way out of Hell or opportunity to seek their Lord’s favour; every hope is closed.
rows.anchor: neither will they be able to come out of Hell nor afforded with the opportunity of seeking repentance from their Lord and win His favour

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from direct to indirect address signals that the threat to ignore them is taking effect and they are unworthy of direct address.
rows.anchor: they are no longer addressed. It is as if the threat to ignore them has begun to manifest itself

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close gathers the argument into praise of God as Lord of all creation and asks why people invent other lords despite being created and nurtured by Him.
rows.anchor: He is the Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of all the creatures of the Universe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone is the universe’s Lord and Master, sovereignty belongs to Him; rebellion challenges His rule and will meet its fate.
rows.anchor: when God is the Lord of the Universe, then in the presence of the real Master and King, how can some other being be regarded as sovereign and exalted?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty so none can escape His grasp, yet wise: His respite is not impunity, and His wisdom will eventually become manifest.
rows.anchor: if He has given respite to people to rebel, then people should not misconstrue this lenience on His part that they are beyond His grasp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author closes the exegesis by attributing its completion to God’s grace and giving thanks for His favour.
rows.anchor: By the grace of God, I come to the end of the exegesis of this sūrah

none: Bare sūrah title page; no commentary point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘Ād ignored warnings of God’s grasp like Quraysh; God destroyed them despite their greater power and more developed civilization.
rows.anchor: showing conceit in their power and might did not pay heed; at last the Almighty destroyed them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn’s response to hearing the Qur’an reassures the Prophet: Quraysh’s failure to honor it reflects hard hearts, since the jinn became ardent preachers after hearing a few verses.
rows.anchor: when a few of its verses were overheard by a passing by group of jinn, they became so fascinated by it that they became its ardent preachers among their nation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s conclusion warns and threatens disbelievers while urging the Prophet to patience and perseverance.
rows.anchor: This is the concluding section of the sūrah. The disbelievers are warned and threatened and the Prophet (sws) is urged to show patience and perseverance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening verses of al-Aḥqāf also form the opening part of the preceding sūrah, linking the two openings.
rows.anchor: Both these verses also form the opening part of the previous sūrah
